strongest_angle: Explore how heavy October 2026 rainfall linked to a Super El Nino weather pattern sent massive volumes of water surging over the Iguazu Falls along the Brazil-Argentina border, causing national park closures and flows up to ten times normal levels.

key_facts.fact: National park officials took the precautionary measure to limit tourist access after heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate in October 2026.

Iguazu Falls, an Unesco world heritage site, has reached a record water flow after heavy rains across the river basin, with El Nino weather patterns driving the flow to hit 10 times the normal amount in October 2026.
The Iguazu Falls span more than a mile across both the Brazil and Argentina border, experiencing a rain-soaked October 2026 linked to the Super El Nino weather pattern.
Rivers swollen by heavy rains linked to El Nino continued flooding swaths of Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay in October 2026, forcing thousands of people from their homes.
